task: NBA Physical Attributes Impact on Career Performance

workspace_files.role: player master: height('6-10' str), weight, from_year/to_year, season_exp, draft_year, draft_round, draft_number
workspace_files.notes: draft_round/draft_number are dtype object: values are '1','2',... or 'Undrafted' -> must use pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce')

workspace_files.role: physical measurements per draft-combine invitee (2001-2023, 18 seasons, 1176 unique players)
workspace_files.key: player_id (== common_player_info.person_id); 26 duplicate player_ids (players measured twice) -> keep latest season; 3 rows with player_id<=0 (invalid ids)

workspace_files.role: one row per draft pick: season, round_number, round_pick, overall_pick
workspace_files.key: person_id (7990 rows, 7866 unique ids -> a few players drafted more than once)
workspace_files.notes: 704 combine player_ids match draft_history person_id; round_number agrees with common_player_info.draft_round, so draft_history is only a fallback / cross-check. organization/organization_type have 19 nulls (irrelevant here).

join_plan.primary: draft_combine_stats.player_id -> common_player_info.person_id (INNER join; 702 matching rows, 691 unique players after dedupe)
join_plan.fallback: draft_history on person_id to backfill missing round_number (0 of the 691 needed it)
join_plan.coverage: 691 of 1176 combine invitees (58.8%) have an NBA player record; the rest never appear in common_player_info (never played / not in this dataset snapshot). 687 of 691 have nba_flag='Y'.

derived_fields.career_span_years: to_year - from_year + 1 (integer years, inclusive). Range 1-21 for matched players -> ALL satisfy the 0-25 validity filter (691/691). season_exp is an alternative (span-1 in median; max 22 league-wide); career_span_years chosen as it is literally 'career span'. Valid-career filter [0,25] drops 0 of 691 matched players.
derived_fields.draft_round: common_player_info.draft_round coerced to numeric. Two invalid cases must be dropped: 'Undrafted' (114 rows) and missing (5 rows) -> no round, plus one row with draft_round == 0 which is not a real round. Valid numeric rounds = 571, values only {1: 337, 2: 234} because the combine era has just 2 draft rounds.
derived_fields.height: combine height_wo_shoes used as the physical attribute (20 nulls can be backfilled from common_player_info.height parsed "6-10" -> 82 in; parses cleanly for all non-null).
derived_fields.sprint_speed: three_quarter_sprint in SECONDS - lower is faster. This attribute is direction-inverted vs height/wingspan/vertical-leap, important when reading the sign of the composite score.

draft_round.note: valid rounds only (1<=round<=2 in the combine era); mean=1.41, std=0.49, median=1 -> effectively binary 1st vs 2nd round

data_quality.implausible_values: none found: no zero/negative heights, wingspans, jumps or sprints; wingspan - height (apex) mean = +5.04 in, consistent with NBA norms; max_vertical_leap 25-44 in, three_quarter_sprint 2.96-3.81 s, lane_agility_time 9.65-13.32 s -> all physiologically plausible (no outlier trimming needed; keep or use plausibility bounds rather than statistics-based cuts).
data_quality.missingness: max_vertical_leap (106 null), three_quarter_sprint (108), lane_agility_time (113), wingspan (19), height_wo_shoes (20) among the 691 matched players. 19 players have all core attributes missing.
data_quality.key_limitation: draft round is effectively binary (round 1 vs round 2) in the combine era, so 'correlation_with_draft' is a point-biserial on a restricted range and slightly noisy - recommend reporting p-values and, as a sensitivity check, the continuous overall draft pick (common_player_info.draft_number, 578 numeric values 1-60).
data_quality.season_exp_note: career_span_years >= season_exp for 100% of players (median gap 1 year, max 7 for players with seasons out of the league) - span counts calendar years, season_exp counts seasons played.
data_quality.direction_note: composite_score = -r(draft) + r(career) assumes every attribute is 'higher = better'. For three_quarter_sprint (a time) the interpretation flips: a negative -r(draft) term for sprint actually favours slower players on this scale. Downstream should flag this in the write-up / plot labels.
data_quality.draft_round_zero_anomaly: 1 matched player has draft_round == 0 (invalid sentinel) - filter draft_round between 1 and 10 (or just >=1).

steps: combine: drop rows with player_id<=0, sort by season, drop_duplicates('player_id', keep='last')
inner merge combine -> common_player_info on player_id==person_id
career_span_years = to_year - from_year + 1; drop rows outside [0,25] (none dropped in practice)

draft_round_num = pd.to_numeric(draft_round, errors='coerce'); keep only 1 <= draft_round_num <= 10 (drops 'Undrafted'/NaN and the single round-0 sentinel) -> 571 players; correlations use pairwise-complete observations per attribute (n between ~400 and ~571)
pearson r + two-sided p (scipy.stats.pearsonr) of each attribute vs draft_round_num and vs career_span_years, pairwise complete observations
figures: 2x2 matplotlib: heatmap (4 attrs x [draft round, career span] correlation matrix), bar chart of normalized weights, scatter height vs draft round (+regression line), scatter max vertical leap vs career span (+regression line)
